thread:
Maya: Heads-up — I uploaded a perfetto + nsys capture for the KV cache HBM spike we've been chasing. Trace: https://perfetto.link/abcd1234 (look at [KB/kv_window] region around t=00:02.1). Quick summary: large seqlen cases (>= 4096) show repeated HBM bursts coinciding with KV miss-driven prefetch + eviction waves.

Josh: Nice, grabbing it now. Is this the same workload we saw last week or a new config?

Maya: Same model + batch pattern, but repro frequency up from ~4% -> ~26% after the batching heuristics change (windowed microbatching). I suspect the windowing exposes long-lived KV pages that thrash with our current LRU.

Raj: I ran a short nsys profile. Topline counters:
```
HSW HBM Read Bandwidth ~ 605 GB/s peak
HBM Write Bandwidth ~ 120 GB/s
SM Active % spikes aligned with kernel conv_kv_tile::read_prefetch
L2 read hit rate drops from 78% -> 22% during the spike
```
Those numbers look like streaming eviction + refetch.

Simon: Can you paste the microbatch sequence at the time window? wondering if prefix reuse is poor.

Maya: Copying snippet from the trace (simplified):
```
[t=02.06s] request A: seqlen 512 -> hotpage 0x7f... accessed
[t=02.07s] request B: seqlen 4096 -> touches hotpage list -> triggers prefetch range [0x7f..0x8f]
[t=02.08s] eviction: free 8 pages LRU -> kernel conv_kv_tile::evict
[t=02.09s] request C: seqlen 6144 -> needs pages -> conv_kv_tile::read_prefetch (miss) -> stall 12ms
```
Pattern: interleaved long sequences cause overlapping prefetch/evict cycles.

Josh: Could be our prefetch window size + aggressive windowed batching causing simultaneous prefetches. We recently increased batch-window to 256 tokens right?

Maya: Yes. Default window was 128 -> 256 in last deployment.

Raj: Quick experiment: forcing prefetch to be serialized (one prefetch at a time) reduced HBM peak to ~320 GB/s in a 30s run. But latency tail increased for those long seq requests. Microbench attached: `nv-nsight-summary.txt` (I pasted the key lines above).

Simon: Interesting. Two obvious levers: (1) reduce prefetch concurrency or add backpressure from KV read queue, (2) change caching policy for long-term pages, e.g., segregate by seqlen (small vs large) or move to CLOCK-Pro/segmented-LRU.

Maya: Also noticed kernel selection change: for long sequences we sometimes pick matmul_fused_v2 which has higher SM utilization but worse memory locality vs matmul_tiled. Could be compounding the bandwidth issue.

Raj: On that point, I sampled kernel timelines: matmul_fused_v2 has longer resident time and issues overlap with conv_kv_tile. Timeline snippet: `nsys timeline` shows matmul_fused_v2 occupying SMs while conv_kv_tile tries to stream HBM -> interference.

Josh: Could we try forcing kernel selection to matmul_tiled for seqlen>2048 and see? That might reduce overlapping HBM pressure by switching to a more compute-bound kernel.

Simon: Yes, let's AB test:
- Variant A: serialize prefetches (limit prefetch concurrency=1) + keep kernel selection diff
- Variant B: change kernel selection policy (force tiled for seqlen>2048) + prefetch concurrency default
- Variant C: segmented LRU + default prefetch

Maya: I kicked off quick runs for A and B on dev-GPU pool. Initial results (30s loadgen):
- A: HBM peak 330 GB/s, 95p latency +18%, 99p +40%
- B: HBM peak 420 GB/s, 95p latency -6%, 99p -3%
- C: (queued)
So forcing tiled reduces tail latency and improves QoS even though bandwidth still higher than A. B looks promising.

Raj: Good find. That suggests kernel interference is a bigger QoS driver than pure bandwidth. If tiled kernel uses less streaming and better L2 reuse, it lowers tail.

Simon: For a production fix I'd recommend combining policies: prefer tiled for long seqs AND add a soft prefetch concurrency cap (e.g., 2) to avoid pathological multi-request storms. Also add an async telemetry counter for "kv_eviction_rate" and "prefetch_concurrency" so we can correlate in Console dashboards.

Maya: Agreed. I'll open a small RFC and a rollout plan. Action items:
- Maya: RFC + perf traces (A/B) attached
- Raj: PoC segmented LRU + perf script (blocked on C run)
- Simon: Add kernel-selection flag and A/B gating in runtime (config & rollout)
- Josh: Create dashboard charts for HBM-bandwidth, kv_eviction_rate, kernel_variant_ratio

perf-bot: ran perf check: "no regressions detected for baseline kernels", but note: experimental tiled forcing needs smoke tests across different models.

Maya: I'll schedule a short sync tomorrow to decide rollout order. Thanks all :thumbsup:
